fieldMarks: Rotund partridge with sandy-brown upperparts, gray breast and buff belly
Bold black band across the forehead and through the eye forming a necklace around a white or creamy throat
Flanks boldly barred black, white and chestnut
Coral-red bill, legs and eye-ring; short tail with chestnut outer feathers
Juveniles are duller and mottled, lacking the sharp head and flank pattern
behavior: Travels in coveys from late summer to early spring
Territorial males give a harsh cackling chuk chuk chukar from rocky cliffs in spring
Feeds mostly on the ground on seeds and leaves (including cheatgrass and Russian thistle seed), berries and, in spring and summer, insects
Permanent resident in its North American range
habitat: Rocky, grassy or brushy slopes in arid mountains and canyons, often grassland mixed with sagebrush or saltbush; introduced cheatgrass is a key element; needs water unless green leaves are plentiful.
range: Native to Eurasia. Introduced and resident in western North America from British Columbia, northern Idaho and central and eastern Montana south to Nevada, northern Arizona, northwestern New Mexico and south-central Colorado; also established in Hawaii.
